scope: Detailed wet-rotor return pump, working section cutaway, inspection-speed control, six component lessons and qualitative head-pressure comparison
hashMethod: SHA256 of sorted relative UTF-8 filenames followed by build bytes; CRLF normalized to LF in HTML/JS/CSS

pump.method: Serial Chrome 1440x1120 DPR1, actual rendered frame count over 3 seconds after warmup. No older-hardware claim.

before.method: Serial Chrome 1440x1120 DPR1, actual rendered frame count over 3 seconds after warmup. No older-hardware claim.

findings: Compared the existing GPT Image return-pump appearance reference with actual front, top, oblique, exploded, individual-component and phone renders. Original procedural geometry; no new generated image downloads.
Added fine mottled polymer grain, ceramic shaft/collars, rubber pads and O-ring, recessed fasteners, helical fitting threads, hollow channels, mounting rails and molded housing seams.
Corrected motor position so the magnetic rotor now sits inside the rotor well, while the outlet remains seated in the whole-system riser.
Section surfaces clarify the removed half; the intact outlet shows the destination of the small round water tracers. Inspected actual rotating-vane frame sequences.
Desktop and 390/320px controls and information remain usable. Inspection speed slows rotor motion continuously. Global pause freezes the rotor and settled scene stops rendering.
Retained all 40 selectable assemblies. Roller, skimmer and live-rock geometry/assets remain unchanged.

limitations: Generic wet-rotor teaching reconstruction, not manufacturer CAD. Fixed-shaft geometry and seven vanes are illustrative.
Qualitative, unitless pump/system curves do not size a pump or predict flow. Inspection speed changes animation only.
Local comparison stays near 60 FPS; it does not establish performance on older hardware.
Section caps simplify the internal shape; this is not a CFD or hydraulic continuity simulation.
deploymentStatus: Local validation complete; production verification recorded separately.
